cap: The transition zone surrounds the urethra, so benign prostatic hyperplasia squeezes it early, while cancer usually starts in the peripheral zone at the back of the gland, where a finger in the rectum can feel a hard nodule. The central zone around the ejaculatory ducts is rarely diseased, and the anterior fibromuscular stroma has no glands. A large smooth gland is BPH; a small hard nodule is cancer until proven otherwise.
teach: Normal prostate glands are tubuloalveolar with papillary infoldings and a two-cell lining, and older men show corpora amylacea, laminated concretions that the seminal vesicle lacks. In BPH the basal cells remain, so p63 stains them. In adenocarcinoma the basal cell layer is absent, so p63 and high-molecular-weight keratin are negative while AMACR is positive. Prostate cancer reaches the lumbar spine and pelvis through the valveless vertebral (Batson) venous plexus as osteoblastic metastases with a raised alkaline phosphatase. TURP removes transition zone tissue, so it neither treats nor prevents peripheral zone cancer.
